video.title: Brooklyn Nets Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Brooklyn Nets for the 2026/27 fantasy season. The big unknown is how Brooklyn handles March: the Rockets control the Nets pick, so they have no reason to tank but also little reason to win, which could cost veterans minutes. His projected starters are Mikel Brown Jr., Egor Demin, Michael Porter Jr., Julius Randle and Day'Ron Sharpe. Porter and Randle are fine draft picks, but he ranks both below their finishes from last season because of usage, trade and minutes risk. Sharpe is his best category-league target, Demin is his upside target in all formats, Brown is a late flyer, and Josh Minott is a stash in deep or stash-friendly formats. He ends with a mailbag answer: auction values on Basketball Monster depend on your league settings, and auction mock drafts carry over to real drafts much less than snake mocks do.

rules.text: The new anti-tanking lottery reforms should make March basketball more competitive across most of the league.
rules.quote: I think it's going to create more competitive basketball in March.

rules.text: A team with no reason to lose and no reason to win in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players. Factor that into the value of its veterans.
rules.quote: The incentive is not there to lose, but for them, the incentive is not there to win either.

rules.text: A player moving from a good team to a bad team does not automatically put up bigger numbers. His usage can rise while his playing time falls.
rules.quote: I don't think it's as simple as from good team to bad team, all of his numbers will rise

rules.text: Some players are worth very different amounts in points leagues and category leagues, so judge their price separately for each format.
rules.quote: But for points leagues, it's too high. And that's the difference. Sharp's value differs between the two

rules.text: Rounds 10 to 13 are the place to take flyers on upside players.
rules.quote: when we're talking about what we do in round 10, 11, 12 of a

rules.text: Rookie point guards are usually bad, especially for their first two to three months. If you draft one who starts, hold him until about Thanksgiving before judging. Some, like De'Aaron Fox and Darius Garland, were never worth rostering as rookies.
rules.quote: But historically, rookie point guards are bad, especially for the first two to three months.

rules.text: Take late flyers knowing you can drop them if things are not working after a few weeks.
rules.quote: we take that flyer in the last rounds understanding that we can be ready to move on

rules.text: Stash candidates matter most in roto, games-cap head-to-head, deep-bench and weekly-lock leagues.
rules.quote: as a stash option in stashable formats roto games cap head-to-head games cap deep bench leagues and weekly lock leagues

rules.text: Auction values depend on the total money available, the number of teams and each team's budget. Enter your budget in your league settings to get correct values.
rules.quote: the prices depend on how much money is available, how many teams are in the league

rules.text: Auction mock drafts do not carry over to real drafts. Once one player goes well under his expected price, everyone's thinking changes and the rest of the draft shifts.
rules.quote: as soon as one player goes $10 under their budget, every mindset changes in the draft.

rules.text: Auction prices change with league size and bench size, so prices from one league mean little in another. A snake draft keeps roughly the same order across leagues.
rules.quote: all the prices are irrelevant anyway. Whereas in a snake draft, there can be slight differences
